item.title: Oxfam's Destroy and Rebuild Index: 'Wealthy minority of investors benefit from both sides of crisis'
item.description: The world's most vulnerable populations bear the brunt and the costs of the climate crisis, while the wealthy and powerful profit. Oxfam France’s Climate Inequality Advocacy Officer Selma Huart examines the relationship between concentrated wealth, unequal exposure to disasters and investors profiting from both polluting industries and reconstruction. “They are burning the planet, benefiting from it, but they are also benefiting from rebuilding,” she explains. Huart places redistribution at the centre of climate policy, calling for taxes on wealthy polluters to finance protection for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Helicopters collide near Mount Everest, killing 1, Nepal Police say
item.description: The helicopters were attempting to land at a helipad in the Solukhumbu district.

item.title: Israeli opposition unites behind Eisenkot as Netanyahu says voters chose him for PM
item.description: Israel's opposition is on Tuesday due to meet for the first time since last week's closely contested election in which neither Gadi Eisenkot's change bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing alliance managed to win a majority in the Knesset. All parties in Eisenkot's camp have endorsed him to be the next prime minister, but the hot-button issue will be whether to unite with the Arab parties who made surprise gains in the vote.

item.title: Under-fire Poundland owner Gordon Brothers defends stewardship
item.description: Poundland's controlling shareholder has told the government it stands by its stewardship record even as it faces mounting pressure over the crisis which has left the discount retailer on the brink of administration.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Voters heading to polls today for midterms
item.description: There are key House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress.

item.title: WATCH: 5 people at Chili's in North Carolina suffer burns after margarita mix-up
item.description: Three customers and two employees at a Chili's restaurant suffered chemical burns after an employee mistakenly used a cleaning powder instead of sugar to make the drinks, health officials say.

item.title: PSG face Villarreal as they aim to keep Champions League top spot
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain are away to Villarreal on Matchday 4 of the Champions League. With three wins from three matches, PSG sit top of the table, whilst Villarreal are 19th.

item.title: US midterms live: More than 58 million ballots cast in record early vote turnout
item.description: US voters head to the polls Tuesday for Midterm Election Day. Democrats widely projected to retake control of the House, though control of the Senate remains up in the air. They will need to gain three seats in the House and four in the Senate to overtake the Republican majority. Losing either will affect President Donald Trump's ability to pass legislation and serve as a referendum on his second term. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: CPJ: 'Attacks on journalists almost always precede attacks on other rights to broader population'
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Jodie Ginsberg, Chief Executive Officer of the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ). The killing of journalists is not simply an assault on those who report the news, explains Ginsberg. It is an attack on the public's right to know, on institutional accountability and, ultimately, on the democratic foundations of society. As the global death toll among media workers continues to rise, a deeper crisis is emerging: the normalization of harassment, intimidation and violence against journalists and the persistent failure to hold perpetrators accountable. “If killers of journalists are allowed to literally get away with murder, that creates the conditions in which we see more and more of those attacks,” warns Ginsberg.

item.title: US carries out 'limited strikes' on Qeshm Island in Iran
item.description: The US military has carried out "limited strikes" on Qeshm Island in Iran - hours before the midterms are due to take place.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Trump signals progress in talks
item.description: The United States reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, even as President Donald Trump signalled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The reported attack was the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out in recent weeks.

item.title: British troops will be allowed to fire at Russian forces if attacked during multinational mission
item.description: British troops will be allowed to fire back at Russian forces if attacked as part of a multinational mission to secure any future peace in Ukraine, Western officials have said.

item.title: European force to hold first Ukraine support exercise in Poland
item.description: Around 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will take part in a military exercise in southeastern Poland from November 9 to 22, testing a multinational force designed to support Ukraine after a potential ceasefire. Led by France and Britain, the force aims to bolster Ukraine's security without taking on an offensive role.

item.title: GOP touts Stevens endorsement while El-Sayed's campaign reports a record haul
item.description: As Republicans touted Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' 11th-hour endorsement of GOP Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers, Democrats downplayed its impact.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares New Jersey students' determination in 100-Yard Food Drive Challenge
item.description: Students at Howell High School filled their football field with over a quarter million pounds of food for the nonprofit, Dermer Dreams. David Muir reports on the volunteers that delivered.

item.title: Europe's Gen Z protesters unite over living costs, housing and employment uncertainty
item.description: Although French high schoolers may have taken the lead in the youth protests that have since spread to Belgium, Germany, Italy, Portugal and Spain, they acted like "a catalyst" for their shared concerns over their future, researchers say, pointing to higher living costs, unaffordable housing and the uncertainty of their employment prospects.

item.title: Russian strikes kill at least 26 in Ukraine after war's longest ceasefire ends
item.description: Russia killed at least 26 people in strikes on a village in southern Ukraine on Monday, including civilians collecting humanitarian aid, emergency workers and police officers. The attack came hours after a rare ceasefire ended, extinguishing hopes of progress towards peace.

item.title: Victims of deadly Florida jet crash named
item.description: A family with two young children and a 20-year-old co-pilot were among those killed when a business jet crashed in a Florida neighbourhood.

item.title: Prepare for cyber attacks or face empty shelves, businesses told
item.description: Artificial intelligence is "helping to industrialise cyber attacks" and is "highly likely" to be used in attacks on Britain's critical national infrastructure by 2028, the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has warned.

item.title: North Korea rejects US allegations over $6 billion Binance crypto heist
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday dismissed US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance as "absurd rhetoric", accusing Washington of seeking to portray the country as a cybercriminal state and warning that US hostility could affect future diplomatic engagement.

item.title: Emergency alerts hacking 'designed to undermine trust in government', expert says
item.description: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyber attacks overnight, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries. The systems have since been brought back under control, though much remains unclear about the attacks, including who was responsible. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr Melanie Garson, Associate Professor in International Security at University College London. She says that these kind of attacks "are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust".

item.title: Woman stabbed while jogging in Brooklyn on life support: NYPD
item.description: The NYPD said the woman had "sustained multiple stab wounds to the neck."

item.title: Trump promised 'no more wars'. His foreign policy tells another story
item.description: Donald Trump promised an “America First” foreign policy and pledged to keep the US out of foreign wars. But since returning to the White House, his administration has been deeply involved in conflicts around the world. From the war in Ukraine and threats to Greenland and Canada, to the US intervention in Venezuela, Trump's shifting approach to the Middle East and war with Iran, Vedika Bahl examines his foreign policy record since returning to office.

item.title: Uganda withdraws troops from peacekeeping mission in Somalia
item.description: In tonight's edition: Uganda starts drawing down troops just days after the UN ends its political mission in Somalia. Also, upcoming municipal elections in South Africa risk solidifying growing political fragmentation. Plus the drought gripping Chad could be the country's worst in more than 40 years.

item.title: How do midterm candidates plan to fight inflation? Economists evaluate proposals
item.description: Proposals include tax cuts and an end to the Iran war.

item.title: The Long Hull: Karl Bushby reflects on perseverance & 'best of humanity' on his 28-year journey home
item.description: "They say it takes a village. In this case, it took a world." After 28 years and some 50,000 kilometres, British explorer and adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his hometown of Hull, completing an extraordinary life journey across four continents that illustrates not only the limits of human endurance, but also the intricate relationship between individual determination, geopolitical constraints and a world of humanity.

item.title: EU says fridge attacks 'deliberate attempt to disrupt' bloc's food supply
item.description: Grocery stores from Sweden to Portugal were hit Monday by a suspected cyberattack on their freezer systems, in what the EU denounced as a deliberate attempt to disrupt the bloc's food chain. Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg and the Netherlands were among at least eight countries affected in the incident, which came three weeks after a cyberattack caused mass disruption in French grocery stores. Food retailers were forced to throw out produce that had spoiled or was at risk of spoiling after refrigerator temperatures soared overnight. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.description: The Election Day Voter Poll helps answer the question of who won and why and explain what issues were important in the election.

item.description: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions. (Image credit: Jon Cherry)

item.title: Is America really that polarized? The answer might be a surprise
item.description: The U.S. has become more politically polarized, but research shows people overestimate their differences and there is 'messy middle' majority of Americans who share overlapping political views. (Image credit: Stephen Maturen/Getty Images)

item.title: Free and fair? The midterms and the state of US democracy
item.description: How far will the president of the United States press this time if Tuesday's midterm elections don't go his party's way? From "only if the Republicans win" campaign promises to a US Justice Department that's already got involved in races, will the White House weigh on the outcome? How will ballot counting go? What's changed since his "stop the steal" rhetoric led to the January 6, 2021 storming of the US Capitol?

item.title: MAGA: Why are Trump's most loyal supporters turning against him?
item.description: Is Trump losing the support of the very coalition that brought him back to power? Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency. And discontent is growing beyond Democratic voters. Some of Trump's most loyal Republican and MAGA supporters are increasingly torn between political loyalty and economic reality. The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base. Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA? FRANCE 24 journalist Stella Elgersma spoke to MAGA and Republican experts to explore how the movement has evolved, what its supporters want and what is driving their discontent. Watch the full youtube documentary : https://youtu.be/XkehRG77itY?si=iOfIl0PwrgyX-j0X

item.title: Israeli 'unity government': Efrat Shapira expects Herzog will urge rival camps to form a 'coalition'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Efrat Shapira Rosenberg, Israeli Radio/TV Host, Columnist, Podcaster and Educator. Following a deadlocked Israeli election, “everyone is saying who they’re not going to sit with, but no one is actually saying who they will sit with.” As President Isaac Herzog prepares to consult parliamentary factions over the formation of a new coalition, the impasse reveals tensions that extend beyond the familiar confrontation between Benjamin Netanyahu and his political opponents. According to Shapira, co-host of the highly popular Israeli politics podcast Miflaget Hamakshavot, the divisions are equally pronounced within the opposition bloc supporting Gadi Eisenkot.

item.title: Russia again pummels Ukraine after rare pause in fighting in Kherson
item.description: Intense fighting between Russia and Ukraine again picked up after a rare ceasefire allowed for a humanitarian mission to reach the war-torn, Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region. While Russia accused Kyiv of sending hundreds of drones toward Moscow overnight into Tuesday, Kyiv said Russia had killed dozens of civilians lining up for aid in Zaporizhzhia.

item.title: French student protests: 'Illiberal' Macron govt dismisses social movement as 'urban violence'
item.description: Jennie Shin is pleased to welcome Éric Fassin, Sociologist and Professor at Université Paris 8. “In a democracy, elections are very important, but it’s not the end of democracy. It’s the beginning,” explains Fassin. He interprets France’s student protest movement growing into a challenge to socioeconomic policy and what he describes as an “illiberal turn” in government. Connecting the treatment of working-class, racialized youth with wider restrictions on dissent, he argues that racism and democratic participation are central to understanding the unrest. His analysis also challenges the attribution of responsibility to the left, placing the government’s response within a broader debate over the normalization of oppressive measures and the far right.

item.title: Trump says deal with Tehran 'could happen' amid 'intensive' talks

Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei shared Iranian plans to reopen blockaded energy corridor, the Strait of Hormuz, if the US were to meet its demands.
